project.name: Bayesian Attack Network Demo — net_28
project.description: Surprise-driven critical scenario discovery for a cyber-physical Bayesian attack network

tool.name: Bayesian Attack Network Sampler
tool.description: Monte Carlo sampling of a Bayesian network representing attack paths through a cyber-physical system. Each node is an attack step; edge probabilities determine how likely an attacker traverses each path. Overall System Resilience measures the fraction of runs where the attacker fails to reach any exit node.

inputs.description: Node yes-probabilities discovered from network_template at runtime
inputs.sme_notes: Entry nodes (low topological depth) are easier to compromise. Exit nodes are primary bottlenecks — their compromise guarantees attacker success. Surprising failures involve mid-graph lateral movement nodes elevated just above baseline while keeping exit-node weights low.

outputs.description: Percentage of Monte Carlo runs where no exit node was compromised (0=attacker always wins, 100=defender always wins)

objective.surprise_definition: Critical attacker success (low resilience) achieved when most nodes have LOW compromise probability — the attacker succeeds via structurally unimportant paths without needing to target the primary high-impact bottleneck nodes
objective.sme_context: net_28 has baseline resilience ~26% and two primary exit nodes that dominate the resilience_delta potential. The richest surprising scenarios involve lateral movement through mid-graph nodes that are on few direct exit paths. The likelihood potential produced CI=0.903 on this network in prior analysis — paths_to_exit is the default but likelihood is a strong alternative.
